comparator.sourceNotes: Current allocation is reconstructed as first year60 + fixed upper-year35 + four alternating-cycle units30 + three concrete seminars15 + thesis10 + genuine open30 =180 EC. The selected legal-French practical seminar and two research seminars meet the current three-seminar/two-research rule. Alternants are counted once across the two-year cycle; Poetry and Theatre10 and Metamorphoses of the Novel5 are explicitly not offered in 2026–2027, so this is a degree allocation rather than a claim that all units run in one year. The adopted formal rules state no specialisation and Dutch/French instruction.

alternatives.concept: Study literature, empire, colonial and postcolonial histories, cultural institutions, media and language/power across global contexts. Treat these as related humanities and social-science approaches while preserving the absence of French-language proficiency and a French-specific literary sequence.

alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical, linguistic and media forms create meaning and express identity and power, combining textual interpretation, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, film and multimodal cultural production.
basisLabels: French and Francophone literature across periods, literary interpretation and text-based research

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film and media; it is labelled as cultural-expression study and not as French proficiency or French linguistics.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. History Research Seminar, European Union Politics and three art/heritage courses are replaced by Rhetorical Communication, Rhetoric in Action, Persuasive Communication, Creative Communication Laboratory and From T.V. to TikTok. The change moves advanced study from colonial history, heritage and cultural institutions to language, rhetoric and mediated expression.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule has 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in year one and ten level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; the only formal prerequisite, Introduction to Brain & Behavior for Psycholinguistics, occurs two semesters earlier. Introductory literary, historical, sociological and film study precedes advanced interpretation, media, heritage and research seminars. No additional French-language prerequisite or proficiency is invented.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass evidence, course-content, schedule and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates. A third French-language proficiency and linguistics programme is not feasible: the workbook contains no French-language sequence, advanced French grammar/phonetics/composition, translation or French-specific linguistic research. Psycholinguistics and stylistics contribute genuine language study but cannot be expanded into or labelled as French proficiency.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both directly study language as an academic object; UCR focuses on psycholinguistic and neurocognitive processes rather than French linguistics.
Both analyse relations between linguistic form and meaning using explicit methods; the external course remains French-specific.
Both directly study poetry and performance through analytical and research-oriented work; UCR is not French-language poetry/theatre study.
The advanced French-language requirement remains explicit; UCR has no French proficiency sequence.
UCR psycholinguistics is aligned once with general linguistics; it does not supply a second French-specific linguistics course.
The B2 French oral proficiency requirement remains unmatched.
The workbook has no French grammar course.
The workbook has no French phonetics/phonology progression.
General academic/rhetorical writing does not replace advanced written French.
Stylistics is aligned once; it does not reproduce the separate French syntax requirement.
The C1 French oral proficiency requirement remains unmatched.
General persuasion and public communication do not reproduce legal French.
Both develop literary interpretation of modern or contemporary texts; UCR is not a French-specific survey.
Both study literature historically across earlier periods; UCR spans a broader Western canon and does not reproduce the French sequence.
Both directly analyse writings of everyday life, memoir and personal narrative; UCR uses cross-cultural life and travel writing rather than French-only texts.
Both connect literature with theoretical or philosophical perspectives through advanced interpretation and research.
The global-literature course does not reproduce the dedicated medieval French and Italian literature requirement.
The workbook has no dedicated Francophone-literature sequence.
No scheduled UCR course supplies this French novel-history requirement.
The selected UCR literature courses do not reproduce this French-language research seminar on the adventure novel.
Both address contemporary social and political change; UCR provides broader modern European/global history rather than a France-specific cultural survey.
Empire and colonial power supply a direct historical relationship to culture and society; the external component remains French-specific.
Media and communication courses are retained as their own credits; none is asserted as the complete external humanities-in-a-digital-world core.
The selected curricula contain no dedicated philosophy-of-science course.
The compulsory French Language and Culture thesis remains separate; UCR optional independent research is comparison-only and not scheduled degree credit.
The genuine approved 30-EC open space remains visible without invented external modules.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives study global literature, colonial and postcolonial history, cultural institutions, media, rhetoric, psycholinguistics and language/power.
